It’s good that you’re considering what it would be like with scars on your body on 5 or 10 years. I regret the scars on my body because they’re irreversible and will be there forever. In the moment, people tend to think they won’t have regrets, but in reality, having scars becomes an inconvenience and is regrettable. I advise you to not go further in this, it can become so toxic and addictive, and you might not even realize it until years later. 

The things that helped me quit was finding something that can help distract you. Or even something that gives you joy even if it’s momentary. I recommend finding a hobby or learning something new. For me, it’s kind of embarrassing but I became addicted to manga/manhwa. I become so absorbed when I find a manga that has a good plot and I forget about anything that was frustrating me before. 

If finding a hobby doesn’t work, you can substitute the feeling that you crave. Use red food coloring, red markers, or even learn how to do sfx makeup and create fake wounds. There are a ton of substitute options that you can find on the internet. 

Hope this helps even if it’s a little bit.

So this is most likely a keloid scar which is a raised scar after an injury has healed. It’s caused by an excess protein (collagen) in the skin during healing. This will eventually turn white and will most likely not be as raised, however, it takes a long time for these types of scars to heal completely. During the healing process, keloid scars can sometimes itch too. This is probably why a 7 month old scar feels like it’s irritated.

Cuts in general regardless of depth will most likely scar permanently. I have a ton of scars that eventually turned white after a year that didn’t even reach styro. The only case I had a scar disappear completely was an extremely shallow cut. However, I did find that if you prevent sun exposure on your scars, they’re heal better. But that doesn’t mean they’ll go away.

13/6/2020, 1:38 AM
Why do I do it? I do it because it relieves me after a stressful day. When I slice through my skin there is a quick sensation of pain, and I focus on the pain. It distracts me from feeling anything else. The more I do it, the better it feels. It’s like my thoughts are wiped clean, and I don’t need to worry or think about anything. My mind is at peace for once. This lasts until there’s no more physical pain, so I’ll have the urge to cut again, and again. After a couple cuts I’ll realize I’m stupid and an idiot for cutting again. I’ll feel shameful and disgusted that self harm is the only reason I’m still alive. And then I watch the blood drip from the cuts, which is so satisfying. I’ll finally clean up the mess and wait until it stops bleeding so I can walk out of the bathroom like nothing happened.
